people.name: Hannah
lines: Wind howls straight up the Monument shaft — climb to the top lookout if you have the nerve.
Stand at the base and look east: the whole green Mall lawn runs unbroken between the museums.

people.name: Sam
lines: South drops to Tidal Basin, west to Constitution Gardens, and east along Pennsylvania Ave to Capitol Hill.

people.name: Arthur
lines: Air and Space still holds its suspended flyer under the glass roof — go on inside.

signs.text: Washington Monument — marble obelisk rising on the west Mall knoll.
Smithsonian Castle — red sandstone towers overlooking the central lawn.
National Air and Space Museum — hangar doors open to the flight gallery.
National Mall Waypost — long elm-lined lawn between twin museum rows.
Mall Ranger Station — trail maps for Monument Grounds and Tidal Basin.
Conservatory Tool Shed — pruning shears oiled for the Mall elms.
Mall Reading Room — glass pavilion facing the Sculpture Garden.
Sculpture Garden Pond — stone bridge spanning the lily water.
Sculpture Garden North — bronze figures mirrored in the quiet basin.
Surveyor's Workshop — brass theodolites pointed toward the obelisk.
Flight Signal Annex — weather vanes ticking above the east portico.
Castle Gatehouse — gravel walk opening onto the long central lawn.
Monument Knoll Steps — fifty empty flagpoles ringing the marble rise.
Monument Grounds Gate — wooded path south toward the Tidal Basin.
Constitution Gardens Gate — calm lake trail west toward Lincoln Memorial.
Pennsylvania Avenue Gate — grand avenue east toward Capitol Hill.
Central Mall Lawn — long west-east greensward framed by neat elm rows.
North Elm Walk — gravel promenade beneath twin rows of American elms.
South Elm Walk — wooden benches facing the central green.
Natural History Steps — limestone columns along Constitution Avenue.
National Gallery Portico — silent dome facing the east Mall lawn.
American History Wing — sandstone facade along the northwest row.
Independence Avenue Walk — southern museum row under flowering trees.
Hirshhorn Terrace — sunken concrete garden along the south promenade.
East Mall Vista — clear sightline from the obelisk to Capitol Hill.
West Lawn Crosswalk — stone path cutting north-south across the grass.
Mid-Mall Crosswalk — flower beds bright between the elm rows.
East Elm Crosswalk — weathered bronze plaques marking the museum mile.
West Monument Meadow — grassy knoll curving down toward Constitution Gardens.
South Museum Courtyard — sandstone arches framing the quiet gallery walk.
Constitution Terrace — broad avenue fronting the north Smithsonian domes.
